subject: Post-call: instrumentation scout & ops checklist for Acme AI evaluation
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Torres <michelle.torres@acme.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: instrumentation scout & ops checklist for Acme AI evaluation

Michelle — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have a single source of truth for the evaluation track.

Highlights from the call:
- Primary goal: validate end-to-end telemetry for inference at 99th pct latency and cost signals (per-model token breakdown).
- Hyperscaler comparison focus: runtime tracing, per-token billing alignment, sampling for cold KV misses, and retention windows for audit logs.
- Shortlist of tests agreed: (1) end-to-end trace correlation, (2) per-request cost attribution, (3) prefix/KV cache visibility, (4) alerting for model regression.

Immediate asks from Acme:
1) A short instrumentation checklist we can run on a 2-hour POC (attached).
2) A sample trace export format so your infra team can validate mapping to existing tracing pipelines.
3) Clarify procurement timeline (cc'ing procurement contact).

Attachments: redwood-instrumentation-checklist.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — high-level steps + what we will observe in Console.
Also attached: hyperscaler-trace-sample-annotated.json (stub).

Next proposed cadence:
- 11/18: 2-hour remote POC (we'll bring an engineer to help wire tracing + sample workload).
- 11/20: sync to compare outputs and finalize procurement scope.

Ben and Sergio — fyi on the checklist; Ben can you confirm who from Infra will join the POC? Sergio please flag any known limits with our trace export formats that might affect Acme's tracing ingestion.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Michelle Torres <michelle.torres@acme.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: instrumentation scout & ops checklist for Acme AI evaluation

Rachel — appreciated the call and the checklist. A few clarifications from our infra side:

- For tracing we need both a Zipkin-compatible export and a JSON line export (sample size ~1%). The sample you attached looks close — can you confirm field names for trace_id/span_id and token_cost fields?
- Our procurement lead asked for an estimate of peak QPS you expect the POC harness to produce so we can provision a test cluster. Looking for a 95th-99th percentile target.
- Regarding hyperscaler comparison: our internal goal is to decide between running on Hyperscaler X managed endpoints vs Redwood Dedicated. We care a lot about per-token cost visibility and KV cache transparency — hyperscaler counters are opaque today.

We'll plan to run the POC on 11/18 14:00-16:00 PT as suggested. Procurement will follow up with a draft SOW and a short NDA redline if needed.

Michelle
Michelle Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme AI
michelle.torres@acme.ai

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: instrumentation scout & ops checklist for Acme AI evaluation

Rachel — I can cover infra for the POC. Quick notes from my side:

- I'll provision a small Dedicated pool that mirrors expected production (8 GPUs, burst to 12). Target synthetic load: 1k QPS sustained for 5 minutes, then ramp tests to 5k QPS for 30s bursts to validate autoscale/fallback.
- Trace export: we'll provide both Zipkin-compatible and a compressed JSONL (see attached sample stub). The token_cost field will be token_cost_usd (float) and per_model_id tags will be included.
- Observability: Redux on what will show in Redwood Console during the POC — per-route latency heatmap, per-token cost histogram, cache-hit ratio over time, and sampled traces with span-level model time.

I'll join the 11/18 session and bring a runtime engineer (Priya). Sergio — can you validate that our trace sampling controller won't drop trace correlation when prefix caching is in effect?

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Torres <michelle.torres@acme.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: instrumentation scout & ops checklist for Acme AI evaluation

Michelle — thanks, confirming the 11/18 14:00-16:00 PT POC. Quick logistical checklist below so the session is efficient: 

Pre-POC (by 11/18 12:00 PT)
- Acme provide IP allowlist and a service account key for ingestion hooks. (procurement@acme.ai)
- Acme infra to share a small sample trace in your JSONL format (we'll validate mapping).
- Redwood to share ephemeral test creds + a short runbook (attached PDF).

POC goals (measured):
- End-to-end trace correlation present for 100% of sampled traces where client sends a trace_id.
- Per-request cost attribute (token_cost_usd) available in trace/span metadata and reflected in Console per-request breakdown.
- Cache visibility: hit/miss ratio + KV cache latency exposed on the dashboard, and ability to correlate misses to spikes in 99th pct latency.
- Baselining: we will produce a short side-by-side of Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler X for the same workload (latency, cost, trace fidelity).

Post-POC deliverables (by 11/20):
- Shared trace exports and a short comparison PDF (we'll call out any gaps for Acme's SRE team).
- Draft SOW for Dedicated that maps to the expected throughput and retention windows.

Attachments: redwood-instrumentation-checklist.pdf, hyperscaler-trace-sample-annotated.json

If procurement needs anything earlier, flag it in this thread and we'll accelerate. See you Thursday.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
